env-merge.reason: A module that owns a binding adds it to `Env` with a declaration merge (step A1.2), and commerce adds its types to two foundation records (step A1.11). Each file that reads `Env` then sees the type of a class above it, and it can call each method of that class with no import. The merges are the design. The methods that a lower module calls are the debt. The check reads no types, so `methods` goes by name and leaves out each doubtful name.
env-merge.fix: Add no merge for a type that a lower module must not see. For a method: the module that owns the part declares its RPC interface (step A1.9) and the caller names that interface, or the Worker gives the call as a port. A method with such a declaration leaves the count.

foundation-misfit.reason: The map places a file by its imports, so a file that imports nothing above the foundation can sit in the foundation. Some of these files hold the code of one area or one surface: a Gmail client, the Slack installation store, the commerce system record. `links` is the rule of check-layers.mjs --misfits. `names` reads the words of the path.
foundation-misfit.fix: Move the file to the area or the surface that it serves, and give the foundation a port for the part that it needs. If the file is general, give it a name with no area word. Then change its line in the map.

table-read.reason: check-layers.mjs gives each D1 table an owner and counts the writes of each other module. A read has no rule. A FROM or a JOIN on a table of a higher module, or of another area, reads the records of that module without its contract.
table-read.fix: Call a read function of the owner module. For a read from below, the owner gives the function through a port. If the lower module is the true owner, change the owner of the table in the map.

surface-nonpublic.reason: The plan lets a surface import the foundation and the public entry of an area. check-layers.mjs allows each area file, because the import goes down.
surface-nonpublic.fix: Import a public file of the area, or make the needed file public in `contracts` of the map. A page or a handler that holds a rule of the area belongs to the area: change its line in the map.

area-package.reason: check-layers.mjs treats each workspace package of an area as the contract of that area. `contracts` lists one package. The others hold a client, a control API, a model or a shared document, and each other area imports them with no check.
area-package.fix: Decide for each package: list it in `contracts` of the map, or import the needed part through a listed contract.

worker-logic.reason: A Worker module composes the three layers and holds no logic. A file there may import each area, so logic that joins two areas was placed there. The count holds each file that is not the entry (a default export), not a class shell (a class) and not wiring (no if, for, while or switch).
worker-logic.fix: Move the logic to the area that owns it, and give it the other area through a contract or a port. Keep registration lines, route tables with no branch and class shells in the Worker module.

shopify-rule.reason: Step A2.5 lets other code reach the Shopify module in three ways: the commerce provider port, the provider module port and their registration in the Worker. No check held this rule. The Worker entry, the Organisation actor and the webhook surface import the module directly.
shopify-rule.fix: Reach Shopify through a port that the Worker registers, as the two registration lines do. The file REMOVE.md of the module lists each importer and what it uses.

interpolated-table.reason: check-layers.mjs reads the owner of a write from a literal table name. A write with the name in a template value has no owner check, and no Actor SQLite table has an owner in the map. The purge, the regional copy, the state machines and the Actor copy code write tables from a list or a parameter. No rule tells a D1 write from an Actor write, so the count holds both.
interpolated-table.fix: Write the table name as a literal where one module owns the write. Add no new general write helper: a helper that must stay (purge, copy, state transition) takes its tables from one list that names the owner of each table.

portal-default.reason: The rule of the whole Portal source folder gives the Portal surface module to each file with no line of its own. So the layer check never refuses a new Portal file, and that file may import each area.
portal-default.fix: Give each listed file its own line or a folder rule in the map, then remove the rule of the whole folder. A new Portal file then needs a line, as a new Platform file does.

contract-runtime.reason: The owner decided on 2026-11-24 that the contract of an area may import any foundation module ("Contracts may use foundation"), so that the public files of each area can move into its contract package as they are. A public file that calls a foundation module above `contracts` at run time ties the contract to the code of that module: the contract then holds behavior, not only schemas and service interfaces. The foundation imports no area, so these imports make no cycle. The count is by area and foundation module, and a contract counts with its area, so the move into the contract package keeps each key.
contract-runtime.fix: A port for each call: the contract declares the interface of the call (a type, or a definePort of @purin-labs/kernel/port), the server of the area or the Worker gives the implementation, and the contract then imports only std, kernel, contracts and types. Then lower the count with --update.
